3.text: the beginning of my acquaintance with the Chukchee tribe I was astonished

4.text: to find that all murders are divided into two categories, those committed

5.text: within the family-group, and those committed outside of it. Only those of the

6.text: second category are liable to blood-revenge. Those in the first category

7.text: were exempt from it, or indeed from any punishment at all. In explanation

8.text: of such a state of things, the Chukchee would even quote something like a

9.text: formula of customary law: “as one of their own he was treated” (činiˊtu liˊg̣nin),

10.text: “as a kinsman he was treated” (čičeˊtu liˊg̣nin). This is meant to express

11.text: that each family-group knows their own circumstances best, and is able to

12.text: decide about them. The Chukchee would add, “Is he destined to live on?

13.text: All the same, he would be killed by a stranger” (Yäqqäiˊ yeˊg̣ telelqäl? Tŭmg̣-

14.text: aˊlvalag̣ ečveˊčä nɪˊnmɪnên). This implies that only “bad men” are murdered

15.text: within the limits of the family-group. In reality, I know this to be true in

16.text: some cases. For instance, in the country of the Oloi River, a couple of years

17.text: before my visit there, a Chukchee by the name of Leivɪteˊhɪn was killed by

18.text: his own kinsmen. He was a man of spiteful temper. He ill-used his house-

19.text: mates, and was even cruel to his own driving-reindeer. The Reindeer Chuk-

24.text: One day, Leivɪteˊhɪn, while on some journey, happened to kill one of his

25.text: reindeer by a misdirected blow. After that his kinsmen resolved to take his

26.text: life. They said, “Otherwise he will be killed by somebody else, and we shall

27.text: have a feud on our hands.” So his own brother came to his camp, and at

28.text: a favorable moment stabbed him in the back with a knife. This act was

29.text: approved by the common consent of all neighbors, because he was a “bad

30.text: one, a source of torment to the others” (eᵋˊtqi tawêmɪn˙ñɪˊɪrg̣ɪn), as they

31.text: expressed it.¹ In another case I mentioned,² a father was killed by his son

32.text: and nephew, with the knowledge of his wife, also for his extreme cruelty.

33.text: Outside of such cases, however, I know of several others where the victims

34.text: were not “bad ones” at all, and the murderers were acting for their own

35.text: material interest, Such was the case of fratricide mentioned above. In still

36.text: another case, a man of the Chukchee country, Yaˊyaq by name, was murdered

37.text: by his nephews in the early nineties of the last century. He was a rich

38.text: reindeer-breeder, and the young men simply wanted to get possession of his

39.text: large herd. On the other hand, Yaˊyaq, a few months before his death, had
